topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening welcome and contextual framing for the lecture on the complement system.

topics.label: Principles, nomenclature, and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the fundamental architecture, naming conventions, and central role of C3 in the complement system before diving into specific pathways.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the three upstream recognition pathways that generate convertases to reach the complement trigger threshold.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the three primary downstream effector processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how deficiencies in individual complement components lead to distinct clinical pathologies and disease vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion strategies and biotechnological applications
topics.groupedBecause: It details how pathogens circumvent complement defenses and how evasion molecules like protein A are utilized in clinical and laboratory settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming topics
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session with closing remarks and a preview of the next lecture topic.
